subject: science
intro: I'm Ms. Johnson. Let's plan a 7th grade lesson on how body systems work together.

beats.narration: Framing systems as a team emphasizes that they interact.
This standard asks students to argue that the body is made of interacting subsystems.
Exercise is a function that clearly needs several systems at once.
beats.text: Students will be able to explain how at least three body systems interact to perform a function, using exercise as an example.

beats.narration: Getting up and moving gives them first-hand data.
beats.text: Students do 30 seconds of jumping jacks, then list every change they notice in their bodies.

beats.narration: Their own observations drive the content.
beats.text: Map their observations to systems: breathing (respiratory), heart rate (circulatory), sweating (integumentary), muscle burn (muscular). Draw the connections between systems on the board.

beats.narration: Different scenarios show different combinations of systems.
beats.text: Groups get a scenario (eating a meal, running from danger, getting a cut) and build a flowchart showing which systems interact and how.

beats.narration: This checks the core idea of interaction.
beats.text: Pick one scenario and explain how two systems depend on each other.

outro: Move, observe, connect, explain. Now plan yours.
